answer: Before an agent can trade, it must present a fresh six-digit IRS Identity Protection PIN, issued only after the IRS verifies a Social Security number against a filed tax return and mails a CP01A notice to the address of record. One PIN per person is a walnut shell no forger can crack cheaply: each fake needs a stolen SSN plus a hijacked filing, about 250 dollars of stolen data and mail fraud, and the quartz-hard test renews yearly. One duplicate filing triggers an IRS freeze that burns the whole batch, while a zephyr of honest agents passes untouched.
